# Context: How much computer music can I get out of really tiny computers?

## Computer music?

- Algorithmically composed and digitally synthesized music

## Wait? How tiny?

- Raspberry Pi Pico W (micro-controller)
- Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W (micro-controller)
- Electro-Smith Daisy Seed (micro-controller with audio hardware)
- Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W (small 64-bit Linux single-board computer)
- Bela Gem (small 64-bit Linux single-board computer with audio hardware)
- Anbernic RG CubeXX (handheld 64-bit Linux gaming console)

## The prime directives:

- Develop interactively ***for*** the device ***on*** the device
- Command line / terminal user interface

# GNU Forth 1.0 (Gforth)

## Basics

- GPL 3.0 License
- Mixed C and Forth code
- All of Forth 2012 standard plus many extensions
- Available for Windows, MacOS, Android, some Linux distros
- Supports mulitple architectures
- Can be compiled for any system with new enough GCC and libraries
- Extensions useful for computer music
    - Cross-compiler: create a Forth for micro-controllers on single-board computer
    - Multi-tasker: use multiple cores, accurate audio timings

## Challenges

- Too big for micro-controllers - needs a cross(meta)-compiler
    - This is the biggest challenge
- Build from source is complex
    - Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W can't compile - not enough RAM
    - Not a serious issue - compiles can run on a larger machine
    - Bela Gem can't compile - not enough RAM
    - Not a serious issue - compiles can run on a larger machine

# The Plan

## Tackle the cross-compilers

- Need two cross-compilers
    - GCC to build Gforth for the Pi Zero 2 W and Bela Gem
    - Gforth cross-compiler for the micro-controllers

## Develop a multi-tasker for the micro-controllers

- Use existing real-time OS and gforth C FFI for Raspberry Pi micro-controllers
- No known multi-tasker for Electo-Smith Daisy
